description.narrative: (USAID Global Health (GH)): .The PSE Kenya Bilateral mechanism will leverage funding from Grand Challenges Canada and other donors to support strengthening Investment Readiness programs (IRPs) for health in Africa. The expected amount to be leveraged is approximately $1.5 M Canadian dollars. These funds will support a network of select IRPs in Africa by enabling to work more closely with potential investors, experimenting with alternative IRP models (e.g., venture studios instead of traditional accelerators) and incentivizing health-specific considerations through targeted technical assistance. .The objective is for IRPs to increase the likelihood of investment readiness among health innovators to attract investors. This work supports scaling of health innovations through an ecosystem (vs. individual company) focus. This builds on recommendations from an IRP landscape analysis in Africa report that USAID and GCC conducted which found that existing IRPs in Africa (publication imminent) lack a focus on health, have limited engagement with early stage investors and need tailored support to be more efficient. This activity will enable CII achieve its localization targets as the mechanism being used is a local bilateral mechanism. It also will enable the development of the IRP ecosystem by supporting the capacity of IRP providers which will increase the number of individuals with technical expertise in investment readiness.
